podcast.title: Active Until the End
podcast.body: Dallas Good and The Sadies were actively playing live and developing new material right up until the day of his coronary illness diagnosis. "Dallas and the Sadies were playing live and working on new material right up until the day of his diagnosis."

podcast.title: Andrew Scott's Hiatus Project
podcast.body: During Sloan's temporary hiatus after "Twice Removed," Andrew Scott performed gigs with The Sadies, pursuing individual musical projects. "Andrew had a few gigs with bands called The Sadies and Makers Mark."

podcast.title: Dallas Good's Coronary Illness and Death
podcast.body: Dallas Good, the singer and guitarist for The Sadies, received a diagnosis of a coronary illness in February 2022 and tragically died a week later on February 17th, at the age of 48, while still under a doctor's care. "Back in February, he got news from a doctor that he was suffering from a coronary illness, a heart condition that he didn't know he had. And then a week later, February 17th, while still under a doctor's care, he was dead at the age of 48."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Esteemed Fanbase
podcast.body: The Sadies and Dallas Good had a respected fanbase that included notable acts like the Barenaked Ladies and Billy Talent. "Fans included the bear naked ladies, Billy Towns and many, many others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Extensive Collaborations
podcast.body: Dallas Good was well-regarded in Canadian music circles and collaborated with numerous other artists, including Gord Downie, Neil Young, and Buffy St. Marie. "Dallas was very liked in Canadian music circles, having worked with many others, including Gordon Downey, Neil Young and Buffy St. Marie."

podcast.title: Formation and Early History
podcast.body: The Sadies are a Toronto-based band that formed in 1994, with Dallas Good as their singer and guitarist. "The Sadies, band that formed back in 1994."

xref.title: Final Public Performance (2017)
xref.body: On February 2, 2017, Gord Downie made his last public singing appearance at Massey Hall in Toronto, joining Blue Rodeo and opening act The Sadies on stage to perform "Lost Together." "And that would be the last time Gord ever sang in public."

xref.title: Extensive Client List
xref.body: His clients spanned a long list of intense indie bands, but also included more mainstream acts such as Bush (for "Razorblade Suitcase"), Cheap Trick, The Sadies, The Stooges, Scott Weiland, Manic Street Preachers, and Canada's Metz. "His other clients included a long list of intense indie bands, but also Bush for Rook Assault, Cheap Trick, the Sadie's Pez, the band that would become Billy Town. The Stuges, Scott W island, Manic Street Preatures, and Canada's Metz."

xref.title: The Bathhouse Recording Studio
xref.body: The Tragically Hip owns and operates its own recording studio, known as The Bathhouse, located outside of Kingston. This studio has served as a recording location for numerous other artists, including Blue Rodeo, Big Rec, Sarah Harmer, Blackie and the Rodeo Kings, Hayden, The Sadies, Kathleen Edwards, The Trews, and The Mahones. "The hip has their own recording studio outside of Kingston called the Bathhouse. Blue Rodeo, Big Rec, Sarah Harmer, Blacky and the Rodeo Kings, Hayden, the Sadies, Kathleen Edwards, the Trues, the Mahones and dozens of others have used the place."
